text:
tara: Heads-up — started a mini-RLHF canary on the new int8 quantized raven-lite model; goal is to reduce hallucination on structured outputs (funcalls).

devon: Nice. Are we running mirroring or mirror+canary?

tara: Mirror + 1% live write-through canary for 24h. Mirror only for metric collection then switch to 1% if no regressions in parse rate.

ellen: Quick note — last int8 rollout (week of 1749995000) showed a subtle suffix noise increase for funcalls. Keep an eye on trailing commas and array ordering.

matt: Can you drop the canary config here? I want to wire it into the telemetry job.

tara: Sure — config pasted below. it's intentionally conservative:

```
{
  "canary_name": "mini-rlhf-raven-lite-int8",
  "mirror": true,
  "live_percent": 1,
  "duration_hours": 24,
  "checks": ["parse_rate", "funcall_accept_rate", "reward_model_delta"],
  "rollback_thresholds": {"parse_rate_drop_pct": 1.5, "funcall_accept_drop_pct": 2.0}
}
```

ci-bot: Canary job created: job_id=canary-7761112222-01. Metrics pipeline subscribed.

deploy-bot: Canary VM shard assigned: shard-7. Start time 2026-03-15T03:12:11Z.

devon: Early telemetry (1h) — parse failures spiked by 0.4% on mirror. Not huge but visible. Raw log excerpt:

```
[03:25:02Z] PARSE_FAIL: invocation_id=ix-9e2, model=raven-lite-int8, reason=non-json-suffix
[03:25:03Z] JSONREPAIR_ATTEMPTED: invocation_id=ix-9e2, heuristics=[wrap-array, balance-brace]
[03:25:03Z] JSONREPAIR_RESULT: invocation_id=ix-9e2, success=true
```

ellen: Do we have reward-model deltas for those invocations? That will tell whether the repair cost harmed quality.

tara: Not yet in the pipeline — matt can you add reward-model scoring on mirror runs? We need before/after RM scores for any repaired outputs.

matt: Adding now. I’ll emit fields rm_score_before and rm_score_after to the canary metrics stream. ETA 30m.

devon: Also observed increased frequency of prefix corruption when kv-cache compression is enabled with the int8 kernel — small probability that the first few tokens include stray whitespace or partial JSON start. Examples: `, \"tool\":` appears before `{`.

ession: Hmm — prefix corruption would explain non-json-suffixs being more common. We should try two mitigations in parallel: (A) runtime prefix sanitization (trim leading garbage up to first `{` or `[`), (B) postprocess conservative repair (only wrap arrays, balance braces, don't coerce types).

tara: Proposal: start with (B) for canary (non-invasive), measure RM delta. If RM delta < -0.02 we stop and try (A) in a new canary. What do folks think? :thinking_face:

matt: +1. Also add a soft flag to log the original output alongside repaired one so we can audit sample failures.

devon: Small caveat — postprocess increases latency for streaming endpoints. We should exclude streaming canary traffic for now or cap postprocess time to 80ms.

ci-bot: Telemetry update (3h): parse_rate baseline=99.12%, mirror_parse_rate=98.68% (delta -0.44%). JSONREPAIR attempts=142, repairs_success=131, repairs_failed=11.

tara: Thanks. Action items for today:
- matt: add RM scoring to mirror metrics + original/ repaired payload logging (in progress)
- devon: instrument kv-cache compression toggles in canary to try a disabled shard if we see regression persist
- ellen: seed small evaluation set through canary outputs and hand-check 50 repaired vs original for quality regressions

matt: I’ll push RM scoring and extra logging, and add a `repair_mode=conservative` flag to the canary config.

ellen: I'll start the 50-sample manual audit; will post examples in this thread.

devon: If after 12h parse delta stabilizes <0.5% and RM delta median >= -0.01 we keep rolling to 5% live for another 24h. If not, roll back to mirror-only and investigate kernel differences.

tara: Agreed. Logging note — include `canary_id` and `repair_mode` tags on all emitted metrics. Also set an alert if JSONREPAIR failure rate > 5% of attempts.

matt: Deployed RM scoring. Samples will show up under metric key `canary.rm.delta` and we'll get a dashboard by EOD.

ci-bot: Canary update (12h): mirror_parse_rate delta -0.38%. rm_delta_median = -0.007. repair_failure_rate = 7.7% (11/142) -> alert triggered.

tara: Alert acknowledged. devon — please flip one shard to disable kv-cache compression and see whether repair_failure_rate drops.

devon: Doing that now. If compression is culprit we should consider a micro-patch to the tokenizer alignment when compression=on.

ession: Also — can we add a regression check against a small golden set where we require identical funcall JSON (no repair allowed)? That will catch silent RM drift masked by repairs.

matt: Good call. I’ll add a `golden_check` sample stream (10k/h mirrored) that fails the canary if any funcall JSON mismatch > 0.25% at 95th percentile.

tara: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. If repair_failure_rate improves after turning off compression we'll iterate a microkernel fix and re-run canary.

ci-bot: Canary paused for shard-7 pending repair_failure investigation.

matt: Quick status: compression-off shard shows repair_failure_rate 1.2% after 30m. Looks promising.

tara: Good signal. Let's roll the compression-off change to the canary config and re-run 24h. Devs, document the tokenizer alignment patch and ship a unit test that reproduces the prefix corruption with compression on.

devon: Will do. Will follow up with the unit test and a short postmortem note if we find kernel bug.

ellen: I'll finish the manual audit and post a summary by EOD.

tara: Closing loop: if golden_check passes and rm_delta_median stays within -0.01 we proceed to 5% live on Thu. Otherwise rollback. :white_check_mark:
